events.headline: Malik Nabers cleared, no designation for Sunday at Philadelphia after a full Friday practice
events.detail: Nabers (knee) missed Thursday, then was a full participant Friday and has no game status on the Giants' final report.
events.so_what: Start him as usual; the full Friday answers the question Thursday's DNP raised.

source.label: Giants.com: Giants vs. Eagles Week 9 injury report (Nov. 6)

events.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) ruled out vs. the Giants; Smith not expected back until Week 11
events.detail: Both miss a third straight game. NBC Sports Philadelphia says Smith will not return until at least Week 11, after the bye. Joe Milton's receivers are Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore.
events.so_what: Bench Smith and plan around two more weeks without him. No single Eagles receiver has claimed the role, and a Milton-led passing game is not a reason to spend FAAB on any of them.

source.label: NBC Sports Philadelphia: DeVonta Smith among those ruled out vs. NYG (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Bhayshul Tuten active Thursday and scores in a 33-10 win at Baltimore
events.detail: Tuten played through the ankle and foot issues that kept him out of practice all week, running 12 times for 29 yards and the game's first touchdown. Trevor Lawrence threw for 242 yards and a touchdown, Parker Washington caught a 50-yard score and Cam Little kicked four field goals. Jacksonville is 6-2.
events.so_what: He handled a starter's carry count on three DNPs, so he stays the lead back going into Week 10. The 2.4 yards per carry came in rain against Baltimore, and the touchdown carried the line. Little's four field goals are the kind of distance-band volume this kicker scoring rewards.

source.label: Bleacher Report: Jaguars beat Ravens without Lamar, box score (Nov. 5)

events.headline: Ravens finalize the Jacoby Brissett trade after Joe Fagnano throws for 60 yards and two INTs in a 33-10 loss
events.detail: The trade became official Friday, per Pro Football Rumors; Arizona restructured Brissett to a one-year, $15.5 million deal to make it work, and Baltimore waived Austin Reed. Brissett could start as soon as Week 10 against the Chargers; the Ravens had not named him the starter when this was checked. Fagnano went 10 of 18 for 60 yards and two interceptions Thursday in his first NFL start, with Lamar Jackson (thumb, IR) and Tyler Huntley (out for the year) unavailable, and Zay Flowers caught three passes for six yards. Derrick Henry is reportedly not seeking a trade, though the Giants and Patriots have shown interest before the Nov. 10 deadline.
events.so_what: Nothing in this passing game was startable with Fagnano. A Brissett start in Week 10 restores Flowers as a weekly start and Mark Andrews as a TD-capable tight end; confirm he is named before moving either back into a lineup. Henry stays a volume back facing loaded boxes until a passer settles in or he is traded.

source.label: Pro Football Rumors: Ravens finalize trade for Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Saquon Barkley cleared, no designation for Sunday vs. the Giants after two limited practices
events.detail: Barkley (hamstring, back) missed Wednesday, then was limited Thursday and Friday and carries no game status on the final report; NBC Sports Philadelphia says he is expected to play. He played 22 snaps to Elijah Mitchell's 39 in Week 8. Joe Milton starts at quarterback with Tanner McKee (rib) questionable.
events.so_what: He plays, but two capped practices and last week's 22 snaps keep Mitchell involved, so he is a flex-range start in this 2-FLEX format rather than an RB1 anchor. Mitchell stays a bench hold, not a Tuesday bid.

source.label: NBC Sports Philadelphia: DeVonta Smith among those ruled out vs. NYG (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Christian Kirk ruled out vs. the Raiders; Demarcus Robinson questionable to come off IR
events.detail: Per ESPN's Nick Wagoner via RotoWire, Evans (Achilles, aggravated in Week 6) is out for a third straight game, and Samuel (hamstring) and Kirk (knee) join him; Kirk may need meniscus surgery, per the SF Standard's David Lombardi. That leaves Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing as the active receivers, with Demarcus Robinson (ankle) questionable and a possible IR activation Saturday.
events.so_what: Bench Evans and Samuel. The thin receiver room should funnel touches to the backfield and tight end. No 49ers fill-in receiver is worth a bid on one week of a depleted room.

source.label: RotoWire: Mike Evans won't play Sunday (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) ruled out at Kansas City; Adonai Mitchell steps into the top receiver role
events.detail: The Jets ruled Wilson out Friday after he entered the protocol Monday following a Week 8 helmet-to-helmet hit. Mason Taylor (back) was limited Wednesday and full Thursday and carries no Out tag.
events.so_what: Bench Wilson. Mitchell and Taylor absorb the targets for one week against Kansas City; that is a one-week bump, not a FAAB-worthy role change unless Wilson's protocol drags into Week 10.

source.label: Arrowhead Pride via Yahoo: Chiefs-Jets Week 9 final injury report (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) questionable for Sunday night at Chicago despite full Thursday and Friday practices
events.detail: Egbuka missed Wednesday, then was full Thursday and Friday, and Tampa Bay still listed him questionable. Gainwell (hip) was limited Wednesday, full the next two days and carries no status. Chris Godwin Jr. and Bucky Irving returned to full practice Friday after Thursday rest days. Kickoff is 8:20 p.m. ET Sunday.
events.so_what: Two full practices make Egbuka a likely start, and the night kickoff lets you confirm at 6:50 p.m. ET inactives. If you roster him, keep a Sunday-night or Monday WR on the bench as the swap.

source.label: Buccaneers.com: Buccaneers-Bears injury report Nov. 6 (Nov. 6)

events.headline: A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson ruled out vs. Green Bay; Hunter Henry questionable after a limited Friday
events.detail: Friday's final report rules out Brown (ankle, knee) and Henderson (illness). Henry (foot) sat the first two practices, returned limited Friday and is questionable; Patriots.com expects New England to lean on rookie Eli Raridon at tight end. Rhamondre Stevenson is not on the report and leads the backfield with Corey Kiner as the spell back. Mack Hollins is also questionable. Henderson said in a Friday statement, per Pro Football Rumors, that he was hospitalized for several days with unexplained neurological symptoms affecting his strength and coordination; there is no return timeline.
events.so_what: Bench Brown. Henderson is an indefinite absence rather than a one-week illness, so he is an IR stash where you have the slot and Stevenson is a confident RB2/FLEX start on volume for the foreseeable future. Henry is a genuine coin flip resolved at Sunday inactives; if you roster him, have Raridon or a streaming tight end ready.

source.label: Patriots.com: Patriots rule out A.J. Brown, TreVeyon Henderson; Hunter Henry questionable (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) doubtful at Philadelphia; Devin Singletary in line to start
events.detail: Skattebo missed Wednesday and Thursday and was limited Friday; the Giants list him doubtful rather than out. Tyrone Tracy Jr. is on IR, leaving Devin Singletary as the primary back if Skattebo sits.
events.so_what: Doubtful is effectively out: bench Skattebo. Singletary is a volume FLEX for one week; he only becomes a Tuesday bid if Skattebo misses Week 10 as well.

source.label: Giants.com: Giants vs. Eagles Week 9 injury report (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle) and George Pickens (hamstring) both questionable at Indianapolis
events.detail: Dallas listed seven players questionable on its final report, including Pickens and Ferguson. KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and Malachi Lawrence (ankle) are out. Ferguson did not practice Wednesday or Thursday; Pickens was limited Thursday. Kickoff is 1:00 p.m. ET Sunday, so inactives land at 11:30 a.m. ET.
events.so_what: Pickens, limited midweek, is the likelier of the two to play; Ferguson after two DNPs is closer to a bench. With a 1 p.m. kickoff there is no late-swap cushion, so line up a tight end in a later window if you roster Ferguson.

source.label: Cowboys on SI: Pickens, Porter Jr. among 7 Cowboys questionable for Week 9 (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) questionable at Miami after three limited practices
events.detail: St. Brown was limited Wednesday, Thursday and Friday and is questionable on the final report. Detroit ruled out five defensive and line starters; RBs Jacob Saylors (neck) and Sione Vaki (ankle) are also questionable. Kickoff is 1:00 p.m. ET Sunday.
events.so_what: He practiced every day, so this leans toward playing; start him unless 11:30 a.m. ET inactives say otherwise. Have a later-window WR on the bench because there is no late swap after 1 p.m.

source.label: Detroit Lions Podcast: Week 9 Lions vs Dolphins Friday game status (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice cleared, no designation for Sunday vs. the Jets
events.detail: Both were limited Wednesday and full Thursday and Friday, and neither carries a game status on the final report. Patrick Mahomes (knee) was full all week.
events.so_what: Start both normally. Kelce is a TE1 in a format where the position is shallow; Rice is a normal WR start with no hedge needed.

source.label: Arrowhead Pride via Yahoo: Chiefs-Jets Week 9 final injury report (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) questionable vs. Cleveland but still on IR; CJ Donaldson ruled out
events.detail: Tyson's practice window is open and the Saints listed him questionable, but he remains on injured reserve and must be activated to play. Travis Etienne Jr.'s window has not opened. CJ Donaldson (shoulder, concussion) is out, and Alvin Kamara (back) is cleared.
events.so_what: Tyson is a stash until the Saints activate him, not a start. Donaldson out and Etienne not back leaves Kamara and waiver claim Audric Estime as the backfield, which makes Estime a cheap Tuesday add only if he gets the clear No. 2 role Sunday.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Final Saints injury report, latest on Jordyn Tyson (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Bam Knight (concussion) ruled out at Seattle; Tyler Allgeier leads Arizona with Jeremiyah Love on IR
events.detail: Mike LaFleur ruled out Knight, plus guards Jon Gaines II and Jayden Williams, on Friday. Love is on IR with a high-ankle sprain (4 to 5 weeks). Allgeier is the lead back.
events.so_what: Allgeier is a volume FLEX start this week behind a line missing two starters. With Love out for weeks, he is the FAAB target in this backfield if still on your wire; James Conner is the handcuff behind him.

source.label: Heavy: Seahawks get injury boost as Cardinals rule out 3 players (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Christian Watson cleared, no designation for Sunday at New England
events.detail: Watson (rib) was limited all week and has no game status on the Packers' final report; Packers.com expects him available. Josh Whyle (concussion) and Micah Parsons (knee) are out, and Chris Brooks (ankle) is questionable and must be activated from IR.
events.so_what: Watson plays, which caps Matthew Golden's target share. A limited rib week argues for a FLEX slot rather than a WR2 lock.

source.label: Packers.com: Packers list three questionable, rule out five vs. Patriots (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Drew Lock cleared, no designation, starts vs. Arizona with Sam Darnold out; Rashid Shaheed ruled out
events.detail: Lock (right elbow) was limited all three practice days and has no game status for Sunday, per John Boyle via RotoWire; he replaces Darnold (quad, cracked rib) for at least one game, with Jalen Milroe the backup. Mike Macdonald called Darnold week to week but he is not going on IR. Lock went 35 of 48 for 422 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions across Weeks 1 and 2, including a start at Arizona. Shaheed (knee) will not play.
events.so_what: Lock is a matchup streamer against a defense he already beat, with the elbow the reason not to trust him over an established starter. Jaxon Smith-Njigba stays a start, since his target volume does not depend on who is throwing. Bench Shaheed. Milroe is a deep konami stash only if Darnold misses more time and the elbow goes wrong.

source.label: RotoWire: Drew Lock set for Week 9 start (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Christian McCaffrey cleared, no designation for Sunday vs. the Raiders
events.detail: McCaffrey (left hamstring) has no game status after limited practices Thursday and Friday, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner via RotoWire. The hamstring limited him to a season-low 52 percent of snaps at Atlanta in Week 7, when he still produced 100 scrimmage yards and a rushing touchdown on 13 touches.
events.so_what: Start him. With Evans, Samuel and Kirk all out, the offense runs through him. Two limited days leave a small chance of a reduced snap share, so Kaelon Black stays the handcuff to keep, not a cut.

source.label: RotoWire: Christian McCaffrey set to play Sunday (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Giants emerge as the most serious Jonathan Taylor suitor; Colts may lower their price to a second-round pick
events.detail: SI's Albert Breer calls the Giants a serious suitor and Fox Sports' Ralph Vacchiano predicts they land Taylor, per Pro Football Rumors. Indianapolis rejected a second-round pick plus another asset while asking for a first or equivalent, but a later report says the Colts may accept a second-rounder. Denver and Minnesota are described as less willing to meet the price. The Giants' backfield is Cam Skattebo, Devin Singletary behind him and Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR. The deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10.
events.so_what: Taylor stays a start while he is a Colt. A move to New York puts him in a backfield with Skattebo, which costs him some volume and costs Skattebo his lead role, so a trade is a downgrade for Skattebo first. Seth McGowan becomes the Colts back to own the moment a deal is official.

source.label: Pro Football Rumors: Giants showing strong Jonathan Taylor interest (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) downgraded to DNP Friday ahead of Monday night vs. Buffalo
events.detail: Jennings was limited Thursday and did not practice Friday, per RotoWire, and likely needs to practice in some form Saturday to have a chance to play Monday. Carson Wentz starts for Minnesota with Kyler Murray out.
events.so_what: A limited-to-DNP slide on a calf is a bad sign. Plan to bench him: once Sunday games kick off, the only replacements left are Monday-night players, so the safe move is a Sunday receiver in his slot unless the Saturday report shows him practicing.

source.label: RotoWire: Jauan Jennings DNP Friday (Nov. 6)

events.headline: Breece Hall (quad) upgraded to a full practice Thursday and says he is ready; Glenn says "both will play" with Braelon Allen
events.detail: Hall practiced fully Thursday after a limited Wednesday, per The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt via RotoBaller, and said he is ready to play after missing five games. Aaron Glenn has said both he and Allen will play. Allen has 504 rushing yards at 5.0 a carry across five starts. Kansas City is the Week 9 opponent.
events.so_what: Hall now looks likely to be active, but a back returning from five missed games into a stated split is a FLEX, not an RB1. Allen keeps standalone value as the back with the current role. Watch Friday for a clean report.

source.label: RotoBaller: Breece Hall logs full practice on Thursday (Nov. 5)

events.headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) ruled out for Monday vs. Buffalo and week-to-week; Carson Wentz starts
events.detail: Kevin O'Connell said Thursday that Murray will not play against the Bills and is week-to-week with a hamstring strain, but IR is not being considered, per ESPN. Wentz makes the start with Max Brosmer behind him and could start beyond Monday depending on Murray's recovery.
events.so_what: Murray is a bench and the rushing premium goes with him. Wentz is a pocket passer, so the Minnesota receivers keep their volume but lose some ceiling. Wentz is a deep-league streaming option at most.

source.label: ESPN: Vikings to start QB Carson Wentz against Bills with Kyler Murray ruled out (Nov. 5)

events.headline: David Montgomery (groin) ruled out for Week 9 and week-to-week; Woody Marks starts at the Chargers
events.detail: DeMeco Ryans ruled Montgomery out Wednesday, his third straight miss since the Week 5 injury, and called him week-to-week, per NBC Sports. Montgomery has 138 rushing yards at 2.7 a carry this year. Marks had 19 carries for 66 yards and a 15-yard catch against the Giants in Week 7, and 15 carries for 56 and two catches for 25 against Jacksonville. Houston comes off a Week 8 bye.
events.so_what: Marks is a volume RB2/FLEX with a poor per-carry rate, so his value is the workload and TD chances rather than yards. Montgomery is a bench hold, with a Week 10 return uncertain. Don't overpay to add a backup in this running game.

source.label: NBC Sports: Ryans says Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 9 (Nov. 4)

events.headline: Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol; Shedeur Sanders takes first-team reps and is the likely Week 9 starter at New Orleans
events.detail: Watson reported symptoms Tuesday morning, two days after a helmet-to-helmet hit in the 26-7 loss to Pittsburgh, per ESPN. Todd Monken did not rule him out but said clearing is "a little more difficult for a quarterback" without practice reps. Sanders has thrown three passes this year; he started seven games as a rookie in 2025 with 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. ESPN's fantasy desk rates Quinshon Judkins a low-end RB2 in a good matchup and Harold Fannin Jr. the most reliable Cleveland pass catcher if Sanders plays.
events.so_what: Sanders has some konami value on scrambles but his rookie turnover rate makes him a streamer only in the deepest pinch, with INTs costing just -1 the one comfort. Lower the wide receivers until the quarterback settles. Judkins holds up best here as long as Cleveland keeps the game close.

source.label: ESPN: Browns QB Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol; status vs. Saints unclear (Nov. 4)

events.headline: Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs "probably on the way out" of Indianapolis, per PFR; Daniel Jones also on the trade radar and Anthony Richardson the hold
events.detail: PFR's Sam Robinson says Taylor and Downs are probably leaving as the Colts sell before the Nov. 10 deadline, after trading Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and firing Chris Ballard. Taylor (eight carries in the 42-7 loss to Jacksonville, fewest since October 2023) has not requested a trade; Denver, Green Bay, Minnesota, the Giants and Seattle have been named in talks, and CBS' Aditi Kinkhabwala was earlier assured Indianapolis wasn't soliciting offers. Downs asked out. Jeremy Fowler reports Jones is on the trade radar, Adam Schefter says Minnesota could consider him, and a $10.51 million injury guarantee vesting in 2027 is a reason to bench him. Shane Steichen said Monday "Daniel gives us the best chance to win right now."
events.so_what: Taylor stays a start while he is a Colt with Dallas next, but a move into a shared backfield costs touches, and a trade makes Seth McGowan the stash to own. Downs is a hold pending a destination. Any Jones exit or benching opens Richardson, whose rushing scores at RB rates under the konami premium, so he is the deep stash here.

source.label: Pro Football Rumors: Colts' Daniel Jones on trade radar? (Nov. 4)
